description: US data center markets classified by tier. Sources: CBRE North America Data Center Trends H2 2024, JLL Data Center Report 2025, Cushman & Wakefield 2025 Global Data Center Market Comparison. Vacancy and pricing reflect realistic ranges for each market tier as of early 2026.

markets.name: Northern Virginia
markets.notes: Largest data center market globally. Severe power constraints; Dominion Energy interconnection queues extend 4-7 years. Land premiums $3-8M/acre.

markets.name: Dallas-Fort Worth
markets.notes: Fastest-growing primary market. ERCOT grid offers faster interconnection than eastern markets. Tax incentives via Texas Chapter 313 abatements.

markets.name: Silicon Valley
markets.notes: Constrained by land, water, and power. Premium pricing reflects latency requirements for tech tenants. Limited greenfield opportunities.

markets.name: Phoenix
markets.notes: APS and SRP are major utilities. Water use scrutiny increasing. Desert climate favors free cooling in winter months.

markets.name: Chicago
markets.notes: Central hub for Midwest connectivity. ComEd interconnection 24-36 months. Cool climate advantageous for PUE.

markets.name: Atlanta
markets.notes: Georgia Power offers competitive rates. HB 1192 tax exemptions renewed through 2031. Strong growth in 2024-2025.

markets.name: New York/New Jersey
markets.notes: Financial services latency requirements drive demand. PJM interconnection queue elongated. Land scarcity forces urban retrofits.

markets.name: Columbus
markets.notes: Emerging hyperscaler market. Intel semiconductor plant anchor. AEP Ohio interconnection faster than coastal markets.

markets.name: Hillsboro-Portland
markets.notes: Hydroelectric power from BPA offers low carbon footprint. Enterprise zone tax incentives. Cool climate year-round.

markets.name: Reno-Sparks
markets.notes: No state corporate income tax. Low humidity favorable for cooling. NV Energy offers competitive tariffs for large loads.

markets.name: Salt Lake City
markets.notes: Rocky Mountain Power provides stable grid. Low seismic risk zones available in valley. Growing behind Meta and Microsoft investments.

markets.name: Minneapolis-St. Paul
markets.notes: Cool climate enables aggressive free cooling strategies. Xcel Energy interconnection relatively fast. Emerging hyperscaler interest.

markets.name: Austin-San Antonio
markets.notes: Rapid growth driven by semiconductor investments and tech migration. ERCOT grid benefits apply.

markets.name: Kansas City
markets.notes: Central US latency advantages. Evergy offers competitive rates. Limited hyperscaler presence but growing.

markets.name: Nashville
markets.notes: TVA provides stable low-cost power. Growing enterprise and edge demand. No state income tax.

markets.name: Denver
markets.notes: Xcel Energy Colorado. Altitude provides cooling advantages. Strategic central location.

markets.name: Richmond
markets.notes: Overflow market from NoVA constraints. Dominion Energy territory. Tax abatements available.
